training_note: Positive-only (no ham): needs separately licensed legitimate messages; masked tokens must be harmonised across sources.
schema: canonical msg-v1 (see docs/REAL_DATA_STRATEGY.md); raw columns listed in 'raw_columns'

label_schema.canonical: scam_type 'spam' -> spam, other types -> scam; no legitimate messages

paper: Fishing for Smishing: Understanding SMS Phishing Infrastructure and Strategies by Mining Public User Reports. ACM IMC 2025. doi:10.1145/3730567.3764431
pii_status: pseudonymised by the authors (<PHONE_NUMBER>, <NAMED_ENTITY>, <URL> ... tokens); over-masking observed; some raw URLs remain
collection_method: Public user reports (Twitter/X, Reddit, smishing.eu, Pastebin, SmishTank) — SMS screenshots transcribed with OpenAI Vision API; scam type, brand and lure principles labelled by GPT-4o
geography: global; sending-network country present for ~33% of rows (IND 3,729 rows, the most common)
language: 66 languages (GPT-4o detected): English 22,078; Spanish 4,639; Dutch 1,945; French 1,163; Hindi 175
limitations: Text is LLM transcription of screenshots (possible OCR/LLM errors)
Labels from GPT-4o: kappa 0.93 (scam type) and 0.70 (lures) vs humans on 150 English messages
time field is free text from screenshots; only ~1% ISO dates, so no reliable temporal split
8,573 duplicate raw texts (validator); 23,256 unique after normalisation
English-keyword collection bias; countries with operator-level blocking under-represented
Includes SmishTank reports: overlaps with the SmishTank dataset
No sender identity, session, payment or outcome
provenance: Original authors' artifact release referenced in the paper's artifact appendix.
name: Fishing for Smishing — labelled smishing dataset (IMC 2025)
